title: Dual-frame joint-motion DP with a goal-independent world-axis grasp stream
coverage_gap: The initial feedback supports A3's treatment of large crossed x offsets: E crossed success is 9/10, versus 0/10 for A1 and A2. Residual A3 failures remain in C-HL (2/10), E-HL (1/5) and E-LL (1/5), all classified only as native_truncated. No failure trajectories are available, so their physical cause is not established. A1's C score (0.95 versus A3 0.90) and same-sign E reliability motivate testing whether world-oriented grasp features can coexist with A3's path coordinates.
reusable_regularity: Reach and attachment geometry should not change merely because the goal changes. Keep every A3 goal-frame feature, action rotation and joint motion target, but add a separate learned grasp stream whose entire input is independent of goal, heading and absolute lateral object position. Its world-axis relative pose, coupling velocity, aperture and quaternion features respect the fixed native finger orientation. A six-channel raw world grasp skip preserves metric current/previous alignment without depending on a learned bottleneck. The common DP can learn how this local information modifies the goal-frame action sequence; there is no hand-written action mixer or stage switch.
dependencies_preserved: A3's full 64-channel path context is unchanged: goal-aligned hand/object/goal/wall vectors, velocities, quaternions, heading, world hand and wall center, half sizes, heights and signed world box-face clearances.

World-oriented grasp relations are additional, not a replacement that discards goal or obstacle dependencies. They do not impose obstacle-free translation or arbitrary yaw symmetry on the complete policy.

The new stream sees current and native-previous hand/object relative pose and motion, both apertures and aperture change, current/previous canonical xyzw object quaternions, heights, horizontal/full distance and vertical separation. It has no goal, wall, time, episode ID, stage label or future input.
The single chunk-start action frame and all deployment semantics are identical to A3. The fourth action is still a scalar gripper command. Only explicitly absent object2 is omitted.

evidence_refs.detail: A1 C=0.95,E=0.50; A2 C=0.85,E=0.50; A3 C=0.90,E=0.90. A3 E cells HH=1,HL=0.8,LH=1,LL=0.8; C HL=0.8,LH=1. All reported failures are native_truncated, not diagnosed grasp or collision failures. q3 selected A3 by the frozen score, not IID or loss.
Parent implementation: chunk-start yaw frame, original 64-channel condition and six joint motion channels retained.
Secondary parent regularity: explicit world-axis hand-object geometry in fixed physical units.
Only exact current D20 for any training targets.
Fixed native gripper/world orientation, two-observation causal history and all declared pose/wall fields. Independent goal and object x factors leave a goal-invariant grasp regularity plausible.
Near-tabletop grasp with fixed finger orientation.
Closing aperture and changing hand-object separation motivate local geometry and aperture-change inputs.
Coupled upward hand/object motion motivates explicit difference of their one-step motions.
Carried object remains offset from hand; preserving both hand and object future displacement targets remains justified.

expected_failure_signature: Hypothesis: a goal-independent world grasp stream reduces sensitivity of approach/attachment to the goal-frame yaw while retaining crossed-E carry gains. A useful result would improve the remaining HL/LL success rates without losing E-LH/HH. This is not a claim that the observed truncations were grasp failures. The hypothesis is weakened if A4 regresses on crossed E, suggesting the added world view reintroduces layout shortcuts, or if residual failures persist, consistent with another bottleneck such as carry/settling or attachment ambiguity. More parameters and latency are an explicit cost; ties still use the frozen latency rule.

required_runtime_fields.semantics: All shared causal observations; same new grasp encoder applied independently to both history entries.
Only source of chunk-start heading. No cache, stage oracle, future, reward or simulator access.

action_frame_semantics: Exactly A3: f=(goal_xy-object_xy)/norm, local x=(fy,-fx,0), local y=(fx,fy,0), local z=world z. Encode [fy*ax-fx*ay,fx*ax+fy*ay,az,grip], inverse transpose for decode. Norm<=1e-5 m uses identity heading f=(0,1). Fixed for both causal observations and the entire sixteen-action chunk. Native translation stays 0.01 m/unit; gripper unchanged. Action4 remains first in joint diffusion, orthonormal rotation preserves isotropic error geometry, no candidate clipping or scripted action residual. Host alone clips world actions and executes four.

training_only_targets.name: future_motion_world
training_only_targets.source: Exact D20 obs[t+k+1,0:3]-obs[t,0:3] and obs[t+k+1,4:7]-obs[t,4:7], divided by 0.1 m.
training_only_targets.definition: Unchanged from A3. Rotate both vector triples with the same causal chunk-start heading in diffusion_targets, append after encoded action4. Padded labels zero; only existing action transitions are valid.
training_only_targets.loss: Unchanged auxiliary epsilon loss weight 0.15, separately normalized by mask.sum()*6 with empty-mask protection. Common action loss retains weight one and mask.sum()*4. New grasp encoder receives gradients through this joint loss; no extra phase, reconstruction or behavior-cloning objective is added.
training_only_targets.inference: Ground truth motion never enters condition or denoise. Host noise generates all ten channels jointly, and only decoded action4 is executed.

support_statistics: None, as in A3. No weights/checkpoints are inherited; this is a fresh common-budget training slot. Deployment state is empty; no training labels are cached on the model.
architecture: Original A3 path features64 + current/previous world object-minus-hand skip6 + learned grasp32 =102 per observation. New grasp encoder is 31->64->32 with SiLU; registered only in build_modules. One untouched common factory U-Net, diffusion dimension10. No A2 four-phase router or action-change labels: that initial design did not improve selection score.
change_summary: One feedback-driven revision of A3, adding A1-inspired world-axis local grasp information through a new goal-independent learned encoder and exact metric skip. Original yaw map, 64 path features, motion labels, auxiliary weight/scale, common loss, update budget and all control semantics unchanged. No extra evidence, training or performance search. Initial A4 files implement this one structural revision; no pre-check code repairs.
